title: KV low-bit cache degradation patterns and mitigation experiment plan
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Goal: Measure quality vs memory trade-offs for low-bit KV cache encodings and define safe runtime mitigation strategies to reduce GPU memory pressure by up to 60% while keeping generation fidelity within acceptable bounds for production workloads. Scope: experiments across FP8 (E4M3 style), INT8 (symmetric and asymmetric), and INT4 packings; compare per-tensor vs per-channel scales; evaluate dequantization noise over long prefix lengths; validate on both decoder-only and encoder-decoder family checkpoints used in our model catalog. Deliverables: experimental matrix, benchmark harness, regression criteria, micro-bench PR for GPU bit-packing kernels, rollout safety checklist, and a release recommendation (runtime-1.20).
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting with Serving Runtime and Applied ML. Agreed to prioritize FP8 and INT8 sweeps before INT4 due to higher risk for generative accuracy.

2025-01-16: Built harness for deterministic replay of production request traces (sampled prefixes, beam vs sampling). Added metric hooks for prefix-perplexity, top-1/top-5 token agreement, and rollout breakage score.

2025-01-22: Implemented prototype quant/dequant kernels in CUDA (bit-packing for INT4 and INT8). Microbench shows 2.8x memory reduction for INT4 packing but 1.1x inference throughput hit without batching optimizations.
2025-01-28: FP8 dynamic-range calibration prototype using sliding-window activation statistics. Observed lower tail-saturation than naive min-max scaling on long prefixes.

2025-02-03: First quality sweep on small (7B) and medium (34B) checkpoints using 5k sampled prefixes. FP8: median token-agreement drop 0.6% and median prefix-perplexity increase +2.1%. INT8 asymmetric: token-agreement drop 1.3%, PPL +4.0%. INT4: severe degradation on long prefixes (token-agreement drop 8-12%).

2025-02-08: Added hybrid scheme tests: per-layer FP8 for self-attention KV + INT8 for FFN-backed caches; dynamic fallback to full-precision on high-uncertainty tokens. Hybrid reduced memory by ~42% while keeping token-agreement drop to 1.0%.
2025-02-11: Safety review with PM and SRE. Agreed to require runbook steps and observable triggers before enabling low-bit KV on Hosted API by default.
2025-02-12: Consolidated experiment results and drafted rollout plan for canary on dedicated pools.
Next steps: Expand tests to 100k prefixes, add long-tail customer prompt set, and finalize GPU kernel optimizations for throughput recovery.
tests_and_results: Test harness: deterministic replay of 50k real production prefixes (anonymized). Metrics: prefix-perplexity, token-agreement@1/5, first-token divergence time, and generation BLEU-like overlap for downstream evals.
FP8 dynamic (per-channel scale): memory reduction ~50% for KV tensors, median token-agreement@1 loss ~0.5-0.8%, PPL change +1.6-2.4% across models tested.
INT8 asymmetric (per-tensor): memory reduction ~33%, token-agreement@1 loss ~1.0-1.6%, PPL change +3.5-4.5%. Noted occasional single-token hallucination shifts in safety-sensitive prompts.

INT4 pack (per-channel with bias correction): memory reduction up to 66%, but token-agreement@1 loss variable 6-14% and prefix-PPL increases >12% for long-context traces. High risk for generative fidelity.
Hybrid configs (FP8 for attention keys/values, INT8 for cached projections): memory reduction ~42%, token-agreement loss ~1.0%, acceptable for best-effort latency/throughput tiers.
Throughput: naive low-bit kernels caused 5-15% latency regressions due to extra unpack work. Optimized CUDA kernels and fused quantize/dequantize reduced overhead to <3%.

Edge-case: repeated-token prefixes amplify quantization noise (feedback loop) causing divergence after ~1024 prefix tokens for INT4; mitigation requires occasional cache rehydration to FP16 or stochastic rounding.
Quality thresholds defined: do not enable a low-bit config if token-agreement@1 loss > 2.5% or prefix-PPL increase > 6% on the protected prompt set.
decision_log: 2025-01-20: Decision to prioritize FP8 dynamic-range methods over static INT8 for initial rollout due to better long-prefix behavior. Approver: Kiran Patel (Lead, Applied ML).
2025-02-05: Approved hybrid attention-FP8 / projection-INT8 approach as candidate default for Dedicated low-cost pools. Approver: Mei Lin (Director, Runtime).
2025-02-11: Rollout gating: require canary on dedicated pools with automated rollback if token-agreement drops > 2% or error-rate increases by 0.5ppt. Approver: SRE on-call and Product.
implementation_notes: Quant strategy: use per-channel scale + zero-point where applicable to reduce bias on skewed activations.
Calibration: sliding window of 16k tokens for scale estimation; decay factor to adapt to distribution shift.
Fallback: runtime will mark cache segments as 'degraded' and rehydrate them to FP16 if a per-segment quality score crosses threshold.
GPU kernels: fused store/load path to avoid separate pack/unpack kernels; leverage warp-level primitives for bit-shuffle of INT4 words.
Memory layout: compressed KV stored in a slab allocator with 64KB chunk alignment to simplify eviction and DMA transfers to CPU when necessary.
Telemetry: expose kv.quant.mode, kv.quant.error_estimate, kv.segment_age, and kv.rehydrate_count metrics to Console for per-route dashboards.
notes_for_pm: Recommend exposing a per-tenant toggle for low-bit KV; include a cost-savings estimator in Console so customers can opt in for Dedicated pools. Provide sample size and safety thresholds in the feature brief.
postmortem_considerations: If a canary shows customer-visible regression, automatically revert KV encoding for affected routes and trigger a postmortem. Track rehydrate_count spikes as primary signal.
